fdroid:app.cliphistory.description:
Keep a calm, searchable history of copied plain text on your device.
• Tap to copy, or choose View to read and select the exact full text.
• Search the entire saved text, including long entries.
• Pause recording, choose a limit from 20 to 500 entries, and clear or delete saved text.
• Undo the most recent single deletion while the recorder remains connected. Clear all cannot be undone.
• Keep one entry per exact text, or skip only consecutive repeats.
• Use light, dark or system appearance and optional motion.
• Use a temporary floating three-entry quick-copy panel or open full history from the tile.
• Choose automatic recovery, reboot resumption, explicit Stop, screen privacy and welcome options in clearly grouped Settings.
• Read saved history offline when the recorder is stopped.
• Keep all stored history encrypted on this device. Optionally save source-marked sensitive text, with automatic deletion that defaults to five minutes.
Requires Android 11 or newer, the primary device profile, and Shizuku API 13 or newer with UserService support, running in shell mode: started with wireless debugging or ADB, or on a rooted phone through Sui with Shell mode, which also starts by itself after every restart. Shizuku-Next, Shizuku or a compatible service is installed separately; Shizuku-Next can start by itself after every restart, and some forks need a compatibility companion. Guided setup covers downloading Shizuku-Next, wireless debugging, pairing, starting the service and granting access. Restart the service after reboot if it does not start automatically. Android 11–12 use manual Quick Settings tile setup; separate Recents-preview privacy requires Android 13 or newer.
No internet permission, account, advertising, analytics or cloud service. Your usual keyboard stays unchanged. History uses private no-backup storage. Screenshots and screen recording are blocked by default and can be allowed. Separate Recents hiding is available on Android 13 and newer.
Text over 64 KiB and unsupported payloads are skipped. Source-marked sensitive text is skipped by default; optional capture and its deletion timer are in Privacy settings. Timed sensitive entries also expire after reboot. Turning sensitive capture off removes saved sensitive text. Indefinite retention requires confirmation. Not every source app marks private text. Encryption protects stored files; text remains readable in the app and Android clipboard while in use. The Android internal clipboard interface can vary across devices and OS updates. Saved sensitive entries stay hidden in the list and quick panel until you open them. Root mode is not supported because Android does not allow clipboard reading from root; on a rooted phone, start the service with wireless debugging or ADB. Work profiles are not supported.
Source and issue tracker: https://github.com/saroo98/cliphistory-android

fdroid:com.flx_apps.digitaldetox.name: DetoxDroid: Digital Detox by Default
fdroid:com.flx_apps.digitaldetox.summary: Grayscale, doomscrolling breaker, app blocker: a boring phone by default
fdroid:com.flx_apps.digitaldetox.description:
Most digital detox apps want you to sign a contract with yourself: no phone for the next X minutes, no more than Z minutes in app Y. A few of them take your money when you break it. DetoxDroid works the other way round. It strips the attention-grabbing tricks out of the phone, so that a calm phone is what you get when you do nothing at all. Nothing to start, no session to survive. The protection is simply on, and you pause it on purpose when you actually need something.
Use your phone. Don't let your phone use you.
HOW IT WORKS
You sort your apps and websites into groups. A group says when it counts: always, at night, weekdays from nine to five. It says how much time its apps and websites get together, per day or per clock hour. And it says what happens then: a short wait before each open, gray, a break when you scroll too long, a lock. Templates get you started, from social feeds to nights off, and everything in them can be changed. If you come from an older version, your rules are carried over as groups.
WHAT A GROUP CAN DO
* Turn gray (and dim, and blur). The color drains out of the apps and websites in the group, from the first minute or once part of the budget is used, and on Android 12 and newer they go soft and blurry too: a feed turns into shapes, still navigable and no longer worth scrolling. This runs from the minute you install DetoxDroid. No computer, no root, nothing to grant.
True grayscale it is not. An overlay can only ever paint on top of the screen, so it drags color and contrast towards a flat gray instead of taking the color out. A red notification dot stays recognisably red. The screen just looks dead, which is the entire point. For the real thing, see SETUP.
* Break doomscrolling. Notices when you are stuck in an endless feed, and counts the short videos you swipe through on Reels, Shorts and TikTok. After the break, that feed stays locked for a cooldown.
* Wait and lock. A distracting app can make you wait a few seconds before it opens, sit behind a blocking screen, or be deactivated outright, launcher icon and notifications included. Once the group's budget is gone, its apps lock until the next window.
* Websites, in Chrome, Firefox and most browsers built on them. Your own list, or ready-made ones for porn, gambling, dating, shopping, social media and video. Links that open inside another app are not covered.
AND AROUND IT
* Emergency Brake. One tap, and for a time you pick every group runs at its strictest: whole screen gray, locked apps stay locked, schedules and pause off. Ending early takes a ten-minute wait.
* Automatic Do Not Disturb. On for as long as DetoxDroid runs. Notifications wait for you.
* Pause Button. From Quick Settings, from your assistant, or by holding a hardware button for two seconds. DetoxDroid resumes by itself afterwards, and a minimum gap between pauses keeps "just one more" in check.
* Commitment Password. Locks groups behind a password, one by one or all of them. Keep it yourself, or hand it to someone who won't give it back the second you ask.
* Screen time. Per app and, if you want, per website; app opens, scroll distance, what the hours are worth. A widget and the notification show today's time without opening the app. The other widget is a launcher that lists the apps you pick as plain text, without the icons your thumb goes for on autopilot.
SETUP (optional, and worth it)
The system color filter is a secure setting: Android hands it only to apps holding WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS, and there is no dialog to tap. Grant it once and the wash turns into real grayscale, with Extra Dim on top, which pushes the screen below the minimum brightness Android normally allows. Three routes: from a computer over adb, on the phone itself through Shizuku (the app walks you through it, roughly five minutes), or in one tap if you are rooted. It survives reboots.
Grayscale, Extra Dim and the screen filter are separate switches. Run one, run all three.
The blur needs Android 12 or ne

fdroid:de.kewl.fullscreendy.name: FullScreendy
fdroid:de.kewl.fullscreendy.summary: Fullscreen kiosk browser for wall tablets, tied into FHEM over MQTT
fdroid:de.kewl.fullscreendy.description:
FullScreendy turns an Android tablet into a fullscreen kiosk display for a smart-home dashboard — and makes the tablet itself a device in FHEM over MQTT.
 Dashboards 
Up to three dashboards, each with its own name, URL, login (HTTP Basic Auth) and certificate setting, so different servers can be mixed. One of them is the default dashboard: it is shown at start and again every time the screen wakes up. The side menu lists them all for switching, and MQTT can switch them too.
 The tablet as an FHEM device 
Battery level, charging state and temperature, screen state, brightness and volume are reported over MQTT. Incoming commands let FHEM speak text through the tablet, play stored sound files, switch the screen on and off, change brightness and volume, load another URL, reload, clear the cache or vibrate. Everything runs in a persistent foreground service that reconnects to the broker on its own.
 Presence and screen 
Camera motion detection wakes the display — the image never leaves the device, only a motion flag is published. Instead of letting Android turn the screen off, the app dims it to black with an overlay, so camera and microphone keep running and a touch wakes it instantly, without a wallpaper flash. Optionally the screen can be turned off completely after an even longer idle time.
 Voice control in the dashboard 
The page can be granted microphone access for speech recognition, and a small JavaScript bridge (window.fullscreendy.textToSpeech) provides speech output, which Android's WebView itself cannot do.
 Built for 24/7 operation 
Periodic reload against WebView memory growth, memory released under pressure, and the display is brought back automatically if Android ever kills the app.
 Why the app asks for these permissions 
• Camera — motion detection only; no image is stored or transmitted.
• Microphone — either wake-on-sound (loudness only, no recording) or voice control in the dashboard. You choose which; both at once is impossible.
• Device admin — needed to lock the screen (cmd/lock and "turn screen off").
• Display over other apps — lets the service bring the dashboard back to the front after Android killed it for memory.
• Modify system settings — real hardware brightness over the full range.
• No storage permission at all: the sound folder is picked through the system folder picker, and the app is granted exactly that folder.
The app only talks to the dashboard and the MQTT broker you configure. The one exception is optional and off by default: if you turn on the update check, the About screen asks api.github.com whether a newer release exists. Nothing is downloaded or installed by the app itself.
Free software, MIT licensed. Interface in English and German.

Do you suffer from the oppressive sanity of rulers, guides, and nondestructive workflows? Break free with Darkly, home of happy accidents and beautiful catastrophes. Release your creativity from the bonds of logic. Madness isn't a bug, it's a feature.
 Darkly does not want to be Photoshop, but it wants to be the best paint app for artists. It has a unique brush engine, and dark arts to help you commune with your imagination.
 Darkly pledges to:
 🛐 Honor human imagination
 ⚛️ Run offline and without a login
 ☯️ Never steal or license your art
 ☮️ Stay free and open source forever
 Dark Arts 
 Veils are where Darkly gets its name; "For now we see through a glass, darkly". They're a special layer that shrouds your canvas in a mysterious way, inviting you to see something that maybe wasn't there before.
 Veils are nondestructive. You can paint as usual, behind the veil, and when you disable it, you'll see the full-res result.
 Veils are essentially fancy shaders, and they are fun toys. But they have practical uses too:
 By hiding fine details, they can prevent premature fixation on detail, freeing you to focus on composition.
 During the sketching / ideation phase, they can help with blank page syndrome and destructive self-criticism by giving you permission to be messy, and explore freely.
 They can also help remedy art fatigue (losing eyes for a piece by staring at it for too long) by helping you see it through a fresh lens.
 Voids are a type of layer that specializes in pulling inspiration from outside sources.
 You can use the Noise void to generate entropy, or Screenshare to stream another app (3D software, movie, or video game) directly into a layer. This is great for hybrid workflows, and situations where you need a quick reference, or want to try out different lighting or camera angles, without having to pose, render and paste over and over.
 Voids support masks and blend modes. They are the natural complement to veils, and a natural integration point for other art programs like Blender, which has its own dedicated void 🧡
 Darkly is in beta. Please report bugs and suggest features in Discord!

Capture your screen in a intuitive and straightforward way without distractions.
 Kooha is a simple screen recorder with a minimalist interface. You can just click the record
 button without having to configure a bunch of settings.
 The main features of Kooha include the following:
 🎙️ Record microphone, desktop audio, or both at the same time
 📼 Support for WebM, MP4, GIF, and Matroska formats
 🖥️ Select a monitor or a portion of the screen to record
 🛠️ Configurable saving location, pointer visibility, frame rate, and delay
 🚀 Experimental hardware accelerated encoding

flathub:io.sourceforge.YSoccer.name: YSoccer
flathub:io.sourceforge.YSoccer.description: YSoccer (formerly Yoda Soccer) is a project which intends to create a new desktop game with the gameplay and the style of the well known Sensible World of Soccer (a.k.a. SWOS). It is however not just a clone, but it expands upon the original formula with new features and improved graphics.

flathub:me.mitya57.ReText.name: ReText
flathub:me.mitya57.ReText.summary: Simple text editor for Markdown and reStructuredText
flathub:me.mitya57.ReText.description:
ReText is a text editor for plain text markup languages, such as Markdown and reStructuredText.
 It supports tabs, live text preview, synchronized scrolling and syntax highlighting.
 ReText can export to HTML, ODT and PDF formats. It is also possible to write custom export extensions.

flathub:net.armatik.Kitsune.name: Kitsune
flathub:net.armatik.Kitsune.description:
Kitsune is a Libadwaita client for watching anime translated by the AniLiberty team.
 Browse the catalog, search for titles, and watch episodes with the built-in player.
 Content (catalog, descriptions, and subtitles) is provided in Russian by the AniLiberty API.

flathub:net.sourceforge.Lifeograph.name: Lifeograph
flathub:net.sourceforge.Lifeograph.summary: Lifeograph is a cross-platform note-taking application that turns entries into structured data
flathub:net.sourceforge.Lifeograph.description:
Lifeograph combines powerful features with a clean and thoughtfully designed interface.
 Your data stays on your device, and built-in encryption keeps privacy at the core.
 With WYSIWYG editing, your entries always appear in their final form.
 Integrated data extraction tools transform your journal entries into dynamic tables and charts.
 Main features of Lifeograph:
 Completely local workflow: all data is owned solely by the user
 Encrypted (with AES256) and unencrypted diaries
 Powerful and intuitive parametric tagging system
 Todo management system
 WYSIWYG rich text formatting (i.e. no separate edit & preview modes)
 Image thumbnails, tables, and charts in entries
 Extensibility via Python with support for editing and running scripts from within the program
 Text searching and replacing with Regex support
 Advanced filtering of entries
 Integrated map for travel notes and route planning
 Live tables that are created on the fly based on the user defined rules which can also be pasted into spread-sheet programs
 Live statistical charts that are created from the values in the tables
 Themes in text editor, including background images
 Favorite entries
 Spell checking
 Links between entries and to URIs
 Automatically created back-links to entries referring to the current entry
 Printing individual entries or whole diaries
 Automatically logs out when not used for some time (to protect encrypted diaries)
 Multiple automatic backups to prevent data loss

flathub:org.koderoots.chatqt.name: ChatQT
flathub:org.koderoots.chatqt.summary: A simple AI chat client for OpenAI-compatible providers
flathub:org.koderoots.chatqt.description:
ChatQT is a native KDE application that provides a simple and intuitive interface for
 chatting with AI models via OpenAI-compatible APIs.
 Multiple provider support : Connect to Ollama, OpenClaw, or any OpenAI-compatible API.
 Simple interface : Clean and intuitive design built with Kirigami for a seamless experience.
 Native KDE integration : Built with Qt/QML for seamless Plasma desktop experience.
 Chat management : Clear chat history and control auto-scroll behavior.

flathub:org.plomgrading.PlomClient.name: Plom Client
flathub:org.plomgrading.PlomClient.developer: Andrew Rechnitzer, Colin B. Macdonald, and others
flathub:org.plomgrading.PlomClient.summary: Grading/marking client for the Plom online grading system
flathub:org.plomgrading.PlomClient.description:
Plom is a system for large-scale marking by humans. It prepares QR-coded test papers, collates
 scanned work, and coordinates a team of graders. This is the graphical interface used for grading
 tests.

flathub:org.srb2.SRB2Persona.name: Sonic Robo Blast 2 Persona
flathub:org.srb2.SRB2Persona.summary: A Persona-inspired mod based on the 3D Sonic the Hedgehog fangame Sonic Robo Blast 2
flathub:org.srb2.SRB2Persona.description:
Sonic Robo Blast 2 Persona (usually shortened to SRB2Persona or SRB2P) is a Persona-inspired
 game with Sonic-themed characters. It features the flash aesthetic of the Persona battle system
 with a hint of mainline Shin Megami Tensei buff system, hundreds of available Persona skills and

flathub:vn.suika3.engine.name: Suika3
flathub:vn.suika3.engine.description:
Suika3 is a high-performance, mobile-first 2D game engine designed for

Package Warnings provides the Collector type and a clean and simple pattern for achieving such logic.  Why Should You Use This Tool?

firefox-addons:2991911.name: Password Filler
firefox-addons:2991911.summary: Auto-fills HTTP Basic Auth dialogs from 1Password. Requires the Password Filler Mac app — macOS only.
firefox-addons:2991911.description:
THIS EXTENSION REQUIRES THE PASSWORD FILLER MACOS DESKTOP APPLICATION. It is a thin proxy that has no functionality on its own. macOS only.
Get the Mac app: https://github.com/andreasisaak/password-filler/releases/latest 
When a website returns 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Basic , the extension asks the locally-installed Password Filler Mac app for matching credentials and fills the dialog before the browser shows it. If the Mac app isn't running, the native browser dialog appears as usual.
 macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer
 1Password 8 desktop app, signed in
 1Password Settings → Developer → "Integrate with 1Password CLI" enabled
 Password Filler Mac app installed (free, open source)
 webRequest + webRequestAuthProvider — detect 401 challenges and supply credentials so the dialog fills silently.
 nativeMessaging — talk to the local Mac app over Firefox's Native Messaging channel; never to any remote server.
 alarms — keep the background script alive between auth challenges so the Native Messaging port stays connected.
 host permissions on all URLs — HTTP Basic Auth can occur on any URL; the extension reads only the hostname of 401 responses, never page content, cookies, headers, or form data.
All credential lookups happen entirely on your device. No data is sent to any external server. Passwords are never written to disk by the extension; they live in your local 1Password vault and are encrypted at rest by the Mac app.
Source code, issue tracker, and Mac app downloads:
